note: Never served. scripts/check-rep-routes.ts sends these to the check route as the learner's answer, and the journey can type them into the answer box. The wrong one fails on any problem of the skill; the right one passes on any, because it says what to do in each common case.
wrong: git stash undoes the last commit. I'd run git stash, and the commit comes off the branch so I can redo it.
right:
It depends on whether the commit is pushed.
Not pushed, and I want to keep the changes: git reset HEAD~1 undoes the last commit and leaves its changes in my files, unstaged; git reset --soft HEAD~1 leaves them staged instead (HEAD~2 for the last two).
Not pushed, and I want the changes gone too: git reset --hard HEAD~1.
Already pushed or shared: don't rewrite history. git revert <hash> makes a new commit that undoes that commit (git revert HEAD for the last one), then git push.
Pushed, but only to my own branch that nobody else has pulled, and I want it gone from the remote too: the same reset as for an unpushed commit (git reset HEAD~1 keeps the changes unstaged, --soft keeps them staged, --hard drops them), then git push --force-with-lease.
Not pushed, but an older commit rather than the last: git rebase -i <hash>~1 and drop its line, or git revert <hash>.
Only the message, the author, or the files were wrong, and it isn't pushed: fix the files, git add them (git rm --cached for one that shouldn't be in it), then git commit --amend (with --author="Name <email>" for the author).
On the wrong branch, and not pushed: git reset HEAD~1 takes it off and leaves the changes in my files (--soft keeps them staged), then git switch to the right branch (git switch -c for a new one) and commit there. To move the commit as it is instead: git branch new-branch for a new branch, or git switch to an existing one and git cherry-pick <hash>, then on the wrong branch git reset --hard HEAD~1.
